standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of a spectral space: quasi-compact, sober, and with a basis of quasi-compact opens closed under finite intersections
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The author's definition earlier in the section on spectral spaces
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the three properties that have to be verified for the product.

core_obligations: Sobriety via closed irreducible subsets: the proof takes a closed irreducible subset Z of the product, uses that its images under the two projections are irreducible, and lets x and y be the generic points of the closures of those images (proof lines 4793-4798).

The generic point argument: if the pair (x,y) were not in Z, the proof produces opens around x and y separating them from Z, which is the step where the generic-point description of spectral spaces is used (proof lines 4798-4805).
Sobriety conclusion: consequently (x,y) lies in Z and is its generic point, so the product is sober (proof lines 4805-4812).

The basis of quasi-compact opens: the proof notes that products of quasi-compact opens form a basis whose members are quasi-compact and that the intersection of two such is again of that form, since the factors are spectral (proof lines 4813-4818).
proof_roadmap: 取乘积中的闭不可约子集 Z，其两个投影像是不可约的，取它们闭包的 generic point x、y；若 (x,y) 不在 Z 中就用开集分离，矛盾，故乘积是 sober。
再由两个因子的准紧开集之积构成基、有限交封闭，得到乘积是 spectral。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the stability of the spectral property under products (author lemma at source lines 4787-4790, label lemma-product-spectral-spaces). The proof (source lines 4792-4819) verifies the two non-trivial halves of the definition: sobriety is obtained by taking a closed irreducible subset, passing to the closures of its two projections and using their generic points to force the pair of generic points into the subset (proof lines 4793-4812), and the basis condition is checked by noting that products of quasi-compact opens form a basis and that intersecting two of them stays in that family because the factors are spectral (proof lines 4813-4818). The statement is used later for products of spectral spaces, in particular for the Stone-Cech material of the chapter. H2.
